title.narrative: Advancing Women’s Engagement: Strengthening Opportunities to Mobilize for Equality (AWESOME)

description.narrative: A 5 year advocacy programme to support women’s movements in Ethiopia, Kenya and Uganda to be strengthened, less fragmented and more representative of diverse groups of women, including women with disabilities. These stronger women’s movements will contribute to strong women leaders at all levels, and the prevention and elimination of sexual and gender based violence (SGBV) against women and girls.

title.narrative: An increase in gender sensitive and disability inclusive coverage and reporting in the media
Number of media spots that promote women’s (including WwDs) rights related to SGBV

description.narrative: Society 2.09: # and type of media pieces which promote women's rights and ending SGBV

comment.narrative: Our baseline survey result revealed that the main sources of information on workplace SGBV in the area are TV (47.4%) and Radio (22.2%). Media plays a great role in informing the wider community and awareness creation, for example, currently there is a popular program on TV and weekly radio program “from police files” in which crime cases are dramatically presented and has wider audience.Our survey also found that 48% of respondents do not received any information related to SGBV and Gender equality promotion, so there is need for significant awareness raising to create space for CSO demands around SGBV and women's rights. Factory managers reported that there is no gender equally promotion media outlet in their respective factories except they heard from mainstreaming media. The key informant interviews explained the importance of community-led awareness raising, which we are addressing through other AWESOME indicators.

This is 1 in tear 1 and 65 in year 2. In year 1: This activity (6.2) was conducted by using Celebrity Girl of Oromia beauty contestant and a winner Ms Tourism Oromia of the 2021. In December 2021, a 1 minute TV spot program (like an advert) was prepared with a local language on Oromia Broadcasting Network (OBN) and transmitted for 5 consecutive days after 8:00 pm news. Prior agreement was made with OBN with terms and conditions. The agreement did not include radio as the cost differs and we focused on visual for the reporting period. The message was “Stride to stop Gender Based violence on women and women with disabilities” . Including the OBN-TV spot one TV show/Discussion session was been on air for the education of the mass and for lobby persuasion purposes. In year 2: We have produced 65 media pieces which includes 4 pieces by miss tourism Ethiopia which was transmitted on Oromia broadcasting Services (OBS) television; two live panel discussion by higher official of Oromia region and transmitted on OBS television; 4 different publications by SWDA head offices and 55 media pieces produced by field offices (11 in each). Media pieces produced by field office includes song, poems, presentation and articles for peer to peer discussion and male engagement session.In regard to impact of the media pieces, an examples comes the yearly online panel discussion on Oromia television in collaboration with EWDNA - The panel discussion is getting many on you tube and two researchers from Addis Ababa university called us to work together on fighting against GBV in the future. The major problem we faced in conducting this activity was to get higher officials on the panel discussion. Most officers or directors are not interested to participate on panel discussion transmitted on the live television. Inflation has impacted the number of media pieces being produced.

"In the Ethiopian context, SWDA does not control the media. Hence, we will approach this indicator in two directions.1.SWDA will prepare media pieces to be published on news, as we have already got invitation from the Ethiopian Press Afan Oromo division to sign a contract and use page weekly for the entire year. Hence, we are reviewing it.2.We can invite WROs to publish media pieces on selected topics pertaining to the proposal.3.We will also count the media pieces produced by media personnel after the training. For the changes we are seeking, we want to see these demands raised through media spaces:i.Community awareness on SGBV is enhanced and GBV incidents reducedii.Law enforcement in actioniii.GBV case reporting become culture of the community iv.Stronger women movement in placev.Platforms are created to enhance networks among elected and women in the leadership positionvi.50% ratio for women in the leadership position at the lower administration exercised "

title.narrative: Increased collective advocacy efforts by women's rights organisation (WRO) actors for policy change and legal reform, national and regional level
Number of influencing spaces attended or facilitated related to SGBV and participation

description.narrative: Formal institutions 3.6: # public debates and national events held

comment.narrative: According to the survey result, Kii and FGD discussants pointed that different organizations have organized different events pertaining to the subject matter. Various discussion platforms were conducted with different community groups, elected women, representatives of different sector offices on GBV and women participation. The planned and implemented activities were to support mobilization, networking and enhance women’s participation. The accomplished activities have created a safe space for different community groups to discuss freely in Year 1

This is 4 in Year 1 and 10 in Year 2In Year 1: The National Regional State level agendas were 1) panel Discussion in collaboration with EWDNA among 20 police attorney, Court, traditional court and WCYA office officials , elected women from regional level involvement, 2) Lobby and Advocacy with 25 policy makers at Oromia Regional level on importance of and inclusion of SGBV problems in school curriculum in Oromia Region to prevent SGBV on girls general and risk with disabilities in particular, 3) Oromia region council elected women on Geneder policy gaps and issues related, and 4) Establish and conduct biannual forum for 40 elected women leaders from Oromia nearby zones (East Shoa Zone, DuKam, Bishofto and Lome woreda) and (Oromia Special zone surrounding Finfine (Sebeta and Gelan)) council members to increase their accountability to voice women's rights and issueIn year 2: A total of 90 public debate and national event was held at region and woreda/project area level. 10 national events (March 8 and 16th day of activism) were celebrated in the five project sites; 10 public debates were held at region level and 70 public debates were held at woreda or project area level. Public debates we have considered here are forums organized at regional and woreda level to create awareness on GBV and debate on existing laws and policy gaps.The main focus of these events/debates was on how to solve GBV, HTP, improve/implement women's right, legal gaps and how to collaboratively voice women's right. Attendant of the debates/events includes government officials (Justice office, attorney, health office and police), WRO (women federation, child and women affairs, disability organizations) and Gatekeepers (Hadha siiqqee and Aba Gada). The main objective of SWDA was to create space for increased collective advocacy of each stakeholder. These activities resulted in increased awareness and understanding of GBV, HTP and women's right. in addition, the discussion identified legal gaps related women’s right and increased collaborative work of different stakeholders fighting GBV
Though initially the target for national and international influencing spaces attended or facilitated was zero, SWDA identified opportunities to influence spaces at national and international level.

The public debates and national events focused on the core issue of SGBVs and increasing women’s participation in leadership positions at all level. Online TV discussion organized on Oromia regional television with key Oromia Region offices and the case of the Sulfuric Acid victim who was released after 5 years from 25 years imprisonment created a big debate and became subject for investigation and action. The policy gap will be clearly identified and reported to the policy makers through the government representatives (Women leaders and regional councils). These all events and promotional roles will highly influence the behavioural change among the communities.
